title: deadset conformance expectation file
description: The language-neutral expectation file of one conformance fixture, expect.json. It names what an analyzer must report and what it must not report, per issue kind and per exemption class, and it binds to each language rendering through one thing only: the fixture-local logical name in each expectation's symbol field, which the rendering's manifest, fixture.json, maps to a file and a line. No field of an expectation names a language; the fixture-level languages array is the one place a language appears, and it names which renderings exist rather than what any of them contains. The expectation list is exhaustive for the target: a finding on a position no expectation resolves to fails the analyzer.

name.description: The fixture's name, equal to the name of the directory that holds it: lowercase words joined by single hyphens.

description.description: One or two sentences on what the fixture pins: the behavior that must be reported and the behavior that must not.

languages.description: The languages the fixture has a rendering for, drawn from the languages field of contract/kinds.json. Every expectation applies to every rendering listed, so every logical name must resolve through every rendering's manifest. An analyzer answers the fixture only when its language is listed.

target_kind.description: The target kind the runner configures for the analysis, which decides the reachability class of every finding. It has no default, as the configuration key it feeds has none.

consumers.description: The logical names of the consumers the runner loads beside the target, each rooted at the directory of that name at the rendering root. Absent or empty means the target is analyzed alone.

closed_world.description: The facts about the world the runner declares to the analyzer before analysing this fixture, drawn from the closed set of two below. consumers declares that every consumer of the target's published API is named by the consumers member above; matrix declares that the build matrix the rendering's manifest holds is every configuration the target builds. A runner sets the configuration key each named fact carries, consumers.complete for consumers and analysis.matrix.complete for matrix as contract/config.schema.json declares them, and leaves the key at its default for a fact the member does not name. Naming matrix also sets analysis.configurations from the identifiers the rendering's manifest declares, because a matrix a run derived is never a complete one. The member is optional and never empty, so a fixture that omits it is analyzed under the open world, where a kind whose precondition is a complete world reports nothing at any position. It is the fixture's declaration rather than any expectation's, because the world is a property of the run the whole fixture is answered under.

expect.description: One expectation per subject, exhaustive for the target. Each names a subject by its logical name and states what an analyzer must report there.

symbol.description: The fixture-local logical name of the subject: a declaration, a member, a file, a dependency line or a suppression entry. It is the key into each rendering's manifest and is never a language spelling; the manifest says what each rendering declares under it. Dotted segments are allowed so a member can be named under its container.

report.description: The code of the issue kind an analyzer must report at the subject's position, drawn from the code field of a live row in contract/kinds.json, or the literal none when the analyzer must report nothing there.

symbol_kind.description: The kind of subject the reported finding must be about, drawn from the symbol.kind vocabulary of contract/finding.schema.json, which owns that vocabulary and states what each value names. It is what lets an expectation pin the subject half of that schema's rule on the liveness relation: a row naming a kind the rule lists as carrying no relation expects a finding with no liveness relation, and a row naming any other kind expects one. Optional on a reported subject, so a row that omits it states nothing about the subject's kind, and forbidden when report is none. The value names a subject rather than a language, and a fixture listing more than one rendering names a kind every listed language declares a subject for, because every expectation applies to every rendering.

confidence.description: The confidence the reported finding must carry, drawn from the reachability_classes field of contract/kinds.json. Required when report is a code, forbidden when it is none.

reachability_class.description: The reachability class the reported finding must carry, drawn from the reachability_classes field of contract/kinds.json. Optional on a reported subject, forbidden when report is none.

liveness_relation.description: The liveness relation that must have produced the finding: reference-counting, where one reference from any declaration keeps a symbol live, or reachability, where only a path from a root does. Optional on a reported subject, forbidden when report is none.

configurations.description: The configurations the reported finding must name, by identifier, drawn from the build matrix the rendering's manifest declares and ordered as that matrix orders them. A finding holds in exactly the configurations in which its subject is declared, so a subject one configuration alone declares names that one and a subject every configuration declares names them all. Optional on a reported subject and forbidden when report is none; a fixture whose renderings declare no build matrix names none.

retained_by.description: The exemption classes that hold the subject back, drawn from the class field of contract/exemptions.json. Allowed only when report is none, because a reported finding never carries a non-empty retained_by; the analyzer's retained-symbol listing must name exactly these classes at the subject's position.

details.description: The members of the reported finding's details the row pins, each named and shaped as the details object of contract/finding.schema.json declares it for the row's report code. Every member is optional and the row pins exactly the members it names, so a runner compares those and states nothing about the ones it omits; the object is never empty, because a details naming no member pins nothing. The member set is what a language-neutral expectation can state: a details member whose value is a position or a stable symbol reference spells one language's own names, which no field of an expectation does, so implementations, write_positions, entry and sides have no form here and the arms below carry the rest under the codes whose details arm names each. A member named under a code whose arm does not carry it is refused rather than ignored, and details is forbidden altogether when report is none, because no finding is reported there whose details a row could pin. A member whose value one language alone spells, a build constraint or a dependency section, is named only by a fixture that lists that one language, for the reason symbol_kind states: every expectation applies to every rendering the fixture lists.

narrower_visibility.description: The widest scope that contains every reference to the symbol, so the visibility the references support: file, package or module. It is what distinguishes two narrowing findings whose subjects differ in nothing else.

excluded_by.description: The build constraint that excluded the file, as the file spells it.

dependency_class.description: The section that declares the dependency, which is the selector a stable symbol reference spells for the same subject.

replacement.description: The right-hand side of the replace directive the finding names, as the module file spells it.

mechanism.description: Where the suppression record the finding reports lives: inline, ignore or baseline.

edge.description: The identifier of the declared cross-language edge the finding reports, as the edges document at the target root spells it.

overlap.description: The external linters or rules that report the same kind in the rendering's language, as the overlap field of the kind's row in contract/kinds.json lists them for that language.

items.description: One linter or rule of the kind's overlap list for this language.
